# Axon

LLM inference for Qwen2, Qwen3 and Llama 3 GGUF models on the CPU and on NVIDIA
GPUs, written from scratch in Rust.

No ggml, no BLAS, no binding crates, no CUDA toolkit at build time: a GGUF reader,
quantized integer dot-product kernels (scalar, AVX2, AVX-VNNI), a spinning worker
pool and a transformer forward pass on the CPU; on the GPU, CUDA C++ kernels that
NVRTC compiles at run time, launched through the driver API (both libraries loaded
with dlopen). About 41k lines of Rust and 4.7k of CUDA, tests included.

Every optimized path is **bit-identical** to the plain reference path on its
device: batched prefill produces exactly the logits that feeding one token at a
time does (on the CPU, and on the GPU against the GPU's own one-token step), and
each SIMD kernel exactly what its scalar twin does. The GPU is deterministic and
close to the CPU but not bit-identical to it (its float sums are split and ordered
differently; `src/cuda/qwen2.rs`). The tests check this, and check against three
independent oracles (gguf-py's dequantizer, Hugging Face's tokenizer, Ollama's
greedy output).

## Status

Works today, honestly scoped:

- Architectures: `qwen2`, `qwen3` (dense) and `llama` (Llama 3.x). The tests use
  Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (Q4_K_M), Qwen3 0.6B (Q8_0) and Llama 3.2 1B Instruct, and the
  GPU tests also the Qwen2.5 1.5B, 3B and 7B Instruct, Qwen3 4B and 8B, and Llama 3.2 3B
  and Llama 3.1 8B Instruct Q4_K_M builds; Qwen3 1.7B (Q4_K_M) runs too. Llama 3's RoPE
  frequency factors and the llama-bpe tokenizer with its BOS token are handled.
  Other architectures, mixture-of-experts models and RoPE scaling (a factor other than 1)
  are refused with an error.
- Tensor types: F32, F16, Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K on the CPU. On the
  GPU every weight matrix must be one of the eight quantized types (F16/F32 matrices are
  refused there). Others load for `info` but can't run.
- Sampling: greedy, or temperature / top-k / top-p / min-p / repeat penalty with a seed
  (llama.cpp's order, ollama's defaults). `gen` continues raw text, greedy unless `--temp`
  is above 0 (reproducible output and benchmarks); `chat` talks to an Instruct model
  through its chat template (ChatML, or Llama 3's) and samples by default (`--temp 0` for greedy). On the GPU
  the penalty and top-k (up to 256) run on the device, so only k candidates come back per
  token; with top-k 0 (off: the whole vocab, as llama.cpp) the logits come back instead.
- CPU: any x86-64 (others build too, scalar only). The default build is baseline x86-64 and
  picks its AVX2 / AVX-VNNI code at runtime, with the same output bits as a `-C target-cpu`
  build (see `src/mv.rs`). Attention and SwiGLU use fused multiply-adds when the CPU has
  FMA and a separate multiply and add when it doesn't (`src/vmath.rs`), so logits depend on
  that one CPU property (on x86: whether the CPU has FMA; other targets fuse only when
  built with `fma` enabled), and are identical across paths (`AXON_SIMD`), batch sizes and
  thread counts for a given answer to it.
- GPU (`--device cuda` or `AXON_DEVICE=cuda`): NVIDIA, Linux only. Nothing CUDA is needed
  to build. At run time axon loads the driver (`libcuda.so.1`) and NVRTC (`libnvrtc.so`,
  `.so.13` or `.so.12`, from the library path or the toolkit's `lib64` under `$CUDA_PATH`,
  `/usr/local/cuda` or `/opt/cuda`), compiles its kernels for the GPU on first use and
  caches them in `~/.cache/axon/cuda` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/axon/cuda`). The driver must
  support CUDA 12 or newer, and at least NVRTC's CUDA major version. A GPU newer than
  NVRTC gets PTX for the driver to compile; one older than every architecture NVRTC
  supports is refused.
  The int8 tensor-core GEMMs (batched prefill, speculative verify) and the tensor-core
  attention need sm_80 or newer; older GPUs run batches through the decode kernels
  (dp4a): correct, not fast. Without a usable GPU, `--device cuda` stops with the reason;
  it never falls back to the CPU silently.
- CPU + GPU: a model too big for the GPU is split (the first layers on the CPU, the rest
  and the output head on the GPU; `--gpu-layers N` to choose). For prompts (batches of
  32 tokens or more) the CPU layers' weights are streamed through the GPU, chunk by chunk,
  instead of running those layers on the CPU (`AXON_STREAM=0`: off).
- KV cache: f16 by default; `--kv q8` (GPU only) stores int8 with a scale per position and
  head, half the memory, with slightly different results.
- Prompt-lookup drafting (`--draft K`, off by default): speculative decoding that guesses
  the next tokens from earlier text (prompt and output) and verifies them in one batched
  pass. Lossless: the same output as without it (greedy, or sampled with the same seed).
- Draft-model drafting (`--draft-model small.gguf`): a small model of the same vocabulary
  (Qwen2.5-0.5B for Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3-0.6B for Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.2-1B for Llama-3.1-8B)
  guesses the next tokens, the model verifies them in one batched pass; equally lossless.
- Serving: `axon serve`, an OpenAI-compatible HTTP server (below).
- Rust 1.89 or newer.

## Quickstart

```bash
git clone https://github.com/HaseebKhalid1507/Axon.git
cd Axon
cargo build --release

mkdir -p models
curl -L -o models/qwen2.5-0.5b-q4_k_m.gguf \
  https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-GGUF/resolve/main/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf

./target/release/axon gen models/qwen2.5-0.5b-q4_k_m.gguf "The capital of France is" -n 32
./target/release/axon chat models/qwen2.5-0.5b-q4_k_m.gguf

# the same on an NVIDIA GPU (the build is the same; the driver and NVRTC are found at run time)
./target/release/axon gen models/qwen2.5-0.5b-q4_k_m.gguf "The capital of France is" -n 32 --device cuda
```

`gen` streams the text to stdout and prints prompt/decode speed to stderr.
`chat` is a conversation: type a message, get a reply, keep going.

## Usage

```
axon <model.gguf>                         same as axon info
axon info <model.gguf>                    print a summary and exit
axon gen <model.gguf> "<prompt>" [-n N] [--draft K] [--draft-model PATH] [--device D]
          [--gpu-layers N] [--kv T]
                                          generation (default 32 tokens; greedy unless --temp)
axon logits <model.gguf> "<prompt>" [-k K]  top-K next-token logits (default 10)
axon chat <model.gguf> [--system TEXT] [--no-think] [--ctx N] [-n N] [--draft K]
          [--draft-model PATH] [--device D] [--gpu-layers N] [--kv T]
                                          talk to an Instruct model (sampled; --temp 0: greedy)
sampling (gen, chat): --temp T --top-k K --top-p P --min-p P
          --repeat-penalty P --repeat-last-n N --seed S   (axon --help)
axon serve <model.gguf> [--host H] [--port P] [--ctx N] [--draft K] [--draft-model PATH]
          [--device D]
          [--gpu-layers N] [--kv T] [...]  OpenAI-compatible HTTP server (below)
axon --help | --version
```

Defaults, as `axon --help` gives them:

- `--draft K`: 0 (off); try 7. With `--draft-model`: 3 (0 = off). The gain is in greedy decoding (`--temp 0`); sampled, it's little or none (measured +0.8 % on 7B at temp 0.8, K=3; slower at K 5 and 7).
- `--draft-model PATH`: none. The draft model runs on the same `--device` (on `cuda` all of
  it on the GPU; its memory is set aside before the model is placed). A model whose token
  table isn't the start of the main model's, or whose end-of-generation tokens differ, is
  refused.
- `--device D`: `cpu`, or `cuda`. A model too big for the GPU's memory is split
  automatically: the last layers that fit on the GPU, the first ones on the CPU.
- `--gpu-layers N` (with `--device cuda`): the last N layers and the output head on the
  GPU, the rest on the CPU (0 = all on the CPU). Default: all of them if they fit with
  256 MiB to spare, else as many as fit with another 640 MiB left for the desktop; an
  explicit N only needs the 256 MiB.
- `--kv T`: `f16`, or `q8` (cuda only; on a split, the GPU layers' cache, so more
  layers fit).
- `--ctx N` (chat, serve): the model's trained context, at most 8192. On cuda, if the
  whole model doesn't fit with it, a shorter context if at least half of it (or 4096)
  fits, else a split.
- `-n N`: gen 32 tokens; chat no limit per reply.
- Sampling: `--temp` 0 for gen, 0.8 for chat; `--top-k` 40 (0 = off, all tokens),
  `--top-p` 0.9, `--min-p` 0 (off), `--repeat-penalty` 1.1 (serve: 1, off),
  `--repeat-last-n` 64, `--seed` a new one each run (gen prints it).

Special-token text in a prompt (`<|im_end|>` and the like) is encoded as plain
text, never as the control token.

`chat` keeps the whole conversation in one KV cache, so each turn only runs the
model over the new message, not the history. On a terminal: `/reset` forgets the
conversation, `/system TEXT` sets a new system message, `/help` lists commands and
keys. The prompt is a line editor: arrows, Ctrl-Left/Right or Alt-B/F by word,
Home/End or Ctrl-A/E, Ctrl-W/U/K to delete a word back or to the start/end, Ctrl-Y
to put it back, Up/Down for this session's history, Ctrl-L to clear the screen. A
line ending in `\` (or Alt-Enter) goes on to a new line of the same message, and
pasted text stays one message, line breaks and all. Ctrl-C stops a reply or clears
the line, never quits; Ctrl-D on an empty line (or `/exit`) quits. Keys typed while
a reply streams wait for the next prompt instead of mixing into the reply. The
terminal is in raw mode while chat runs, so Ctrl-Z and Ctrl-\ do nothing. Piped,
each line of stdin is a message and each reply one block of stdout. When the
conversation outgrows `--ctx` (default: the model's, at most 8192), the oldest exchanges are forgotten.

Llama 3 uses the official 3.1/3.2 template (no tools): a system block that always
opens with the template's "Cutting Knowledge Date: December 2023 / Today Date: 26 Jul
2024" lines (its default date, so a conversation doesn't depend on the day) and then
`--system`'s text if any, headers around each message, `<|eot_id|>` ending each turn.

Qwen3 follows its own template: no system message unless `--system` gives one, and
the model reasons first (`<think>...</think>`, shown as it streams; Ollama's default
too). `--no-think` opens each reply with an empty reasoning block instead (the
template's `enable_thinking=false`). Earlier replies stay in the conversation
without their reasoning, as the template renders them. Qwen recommends sampling
for thinking mode (temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20), as `chat` does by default with
its own defaults (`--temp 0.8 --top-k 40 --top-p 0.9`); with `--temp 0` (greedy) long
reasoning can loop.

### Serving: `axon serve`

```bash
axon serve models/qwen2.5-7b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf --device cuda --port 8080
curl -N localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hi!"}],"stream":true}'
```

An OpenAI-compatible HTTP/1.1 server (any OpenAI client works with
`base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1"`): `GET /v1/models`, `POST /v1/chat/completions`,
`POST /v1/completions` (raw text, no template, as `gen`), `GET /health`; streamed
(server-sent events, `data: [DONE]` at the end; `stream_options.include_usage` adds a
usage chunk) or whole. It takes the device, `--ctx`, `--kv`, `--gpu-layers` and `--draft`
flags of `chat`, plus `--host` (default 127.0.0.1), `--port` (default 8080), `--alias NAME`
(another model name to answer to), `--max-tokens N` (a cap on any request's generation;
default: up to the context), `--cors [ORIGIN]` (answer CORS preflights and allow ORIGIN,
default `*`, to call the server from web pages; off by default, so an arbitrary page can't
use your local model), `--max-conns N` / `--max-queue N` (defaults 256 / 128), `--quiet`
(no per-request line on stderr). `GET /health` is 503 until the model is loaded.

- One request at a time: requests queue and run in arrival order, each exactly as `gen` /
  `chat` would run it (greedy `/v1/completions` output is byte-identical to `axon gen`'s).
  The KV cache carries over between requests: a prompt that starts with the previous
  request's tokens (a chat follow-up resending the conversation, a shared system prompt)
  only runs the model over the rest (`usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`).
- Chat prompts are framed as `axon chat` frames them (ChatML, or Llama 3's template with its
  BOS and system block; Qwen2.5's default system message when none is given; Qwen3 earlier
  replies without their reasoning), and end on the same tokens (Llama 3: `<|eot_id|>` too).
  `/v1/completions` tokenizes and stops as `gen` does (BOS for Llama 3). Qwen3 thinks
  unless `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` (or `--no-think` as the server
  default); the reasoning comes as `reasoning_content`, apart from `content`
  (`--think-inline` leaves the `<think>` block in `content`).
- Sampling: `temperature` (0 = greedy), `top_p`, `seed`, and the common extensions `top_k`,
  `min_p`, `repetition_penalty` (or `repeat_penalty`) and `repeat_last_n`; `max_tokens` (or
  `max_completion_tokens`), `stop` (up to 16 strings, not included in the output). What a
  request leaves out comes from the server's sampling flags, else `chat`'s defaults
  (temperature 0.8, top-k 40, top-p 0.9) but with no repeat penalty (1.0, as OpenAI and
  llama-server: `chat`'s 1.1 would quietly penalize the punctuation and indentation of code
  and JSON; `--repeat-penalty` or a request's `repetition_penalty` turns it on). For Qwen3's
  thinking mode Qwen recommends temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20 (greedy can loop on
  long reasoning).
  `presence_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` other than 0, `n` > 1, `logprobs`, `tools`,
  `logit_bias` and JSON `response_format` are refused with a 400 rather than ignored.
- `finish_reason` is `stop` (end token or stop string) or `length`; `usage` counts tokens;
  a `timings` object gives prompt and generation speed (llama-server's field names).
- A client that disconnects stops its generation within one token.
- Limits: 16 KiB of request head, 1 MiB of body (`Content-Length` or chunked), 256
  connections, 128 queued requests (more: 503); keep-alive and pipelining; idle connections
  close after 30 s. No TLS or HTTP/2: put a reverse proxy in front to expose it beyond
  localhost.
- If the engine fails on a request (a CUDA error is sticky: every later request would fail
  too), the server logs the error and exits with code 70, for a supervisor to restart it.

### Environment

| variable | effect |
|---|---|
| `AXON_THREADS=N` | worker threads (default: cores minus a quarter) |
| `AXON_SIMD=scalar\|avx2\|vnni` | force a kernel set (default: the best the CPU has) |
| `AXON_POOL_ADAPT=0` | keep every worker in every job (no adaptive drop-out under load) |
| `AXON_POOL_DEBUG=1` | `gen`: print thread-pool stats at the end |
| `AXON_MMAP=0\|1` | CPU: `0`: copy the model into huge-page memory; `1`: map the file. Default: map it when every weight matrix is repacked (Q4_K/Q6_K/Q5_0/Q8_0 models: the repack holds them in huge pages, so a copy would only be a second pass over the file), else copy unless the file is over 60% of available memory. A mapped model stays mapped while axon runs: overwriting the GGUF in place meanwhile (e.g. `curl -o` onto the same file) can crash it with SIGBUS; use `AXON_MMAP=0`, or write a new file and rename it over the old one. The GPU always maps (it reads the file once) |
| `AXON_READAHEAD=0` | `gen`/`chat`: don't read a mapped model into the page cache ahead of use on a background thread (on by default unless the file is over half of available memory) |
| `AXON_PREFETCH=N` | decode: software prefetch distance in bytes (default 8192, 0 = off, max 1 MiB) |
| `AXON_DECODE_ROWS=1\|2\|4` | decode: rows per kernel call (default 4; K-quants use at most 2) |
| `AXON_REPACK=0` | CPU: run every matrix in place from the GGUF's blocks instead of repacking Q4_K/Q6_K/Q5_0/Q8_0 for the faster kernels (for comparisons) |
| `AXON_DRAFT=K` | same as `--draft K` (gen, chat, serve): prompt-lookup speculative decoding, up to K draft tokens per step (default 0 = off; try 7). Lossless: same output as without it (greedy, or sampled with the same seed) |
| `AXON_DRAFT_MODEL=PATH` | same as `--draft-model PATH` (gen, chat, serve) |
| `AXON_DEVICE=cpu\|cuda` | same as `--device` (default `cpu`) |
| `AXON_GPU_LAYERS=N` | same as `--gpu-layers N` (with `--device cuda`) |
| `AXON_KV=f16\|f32\|q8` | KV cache type (default f16; `f32` CPU only, for A/B; `q8` cuda only, as `--kv q8`) |
| `AXON_STREAM=0` | split model: don't stream the CPU layers' weights through the GPU for prefill batches (default on: they are copied over once per prompt chunk, and those layers then get the GPU's numerics) |
| `AXON_STREAM_MIN=N` | split model: smallest prefill batch streamed (default 32). Streaming pins the CPU layers' KV cache in RAM |
| `AXON_STREAM_DECODE=1` | split model, experiment: stream one-token decode steps too (slower; refused with `--draft`) |
| `AXON_CUDA_GRAPHS=0` | cuda: launch each token's kernels one by one instead of replaying a captured CUDA graph (same results, slower) |
| `AXON_CUDA_PDL=0` | cuda: no programmatic dependent launch (used only on sm_90+ with a CUDA 12.3+ driver) |
| `AXON_GATE_UP=0` | cuda: run the FFN's gate and up products (both Q4_K) as two GEMMs instead of one fused launch in batched passes (same bits) |
| `AXON_Q6K8=0\|1` | cuda: `0` never makes the int8 copy of Q6_K matrices that speeds up prefill (sm_80+); `1` makes it whenever it fits beside the cache. Default: only if 768 MiB stay free beside it and the cache, and never on a split (same bits either way) |
| `AXON_SKIP_MODEL_TESTS=1` | tests: skip the ones that need the real model |

## How it works

Read in this order:

1. **`src/gguf.rs`**: the file format. A header, key/value metadata, a tensor
   table, then the raw tensor bytes, used in place (never converted).
2. **`src/quant.rs`**: block formats and dequantization, then the scalar dot
   products (`dot_*_q8`, quantized weights times 8-bit activations). Read those;
   the SIMD versions below them compute the same sums and can wait.
3. **`src/model.rs`, `hidden()`**: the whole transformer for one token in
   numbered steps (norm, QKV, RoPE, KV cache, attention, output projection,
   SwiGLU FFN, residuals). Then `feed_batch`, the same math for 64 prompt
   tokens at once, reading each weight row once per batch.
4. **`src/main.rs`, `run_lm`**: encode the prompt, prefill in batches, then
   `generate`: `forward`, pick the next token (argmax, or `sample.rs`), repeat.

`pool.rs` (the worker pool) and `tokenizer.rs` (byte-level BPE) can be read
any time.

The GPU, after that:

5. **`src/lm.rs`**: the `Lm` trait (`forward`, `feed_batch`, `verify_argmax`, ...)
   that generation, chat and the server are written against, and `Backend`, which
   holds the CPU, GPU or split model the command line picked.
6. **`src/cuda/qwen2.rs`** and **`decode.cu`**: the model on the GPU. Weights are
   uploaded once in their GGUF block formats; one token is a fixed sequence of kernels
   per layer, captured once into a CUDA graph and replayed every token.
7. **`src/cuda/qwen2/batch.rs`** and **`prefill.cu`**: batched passes (prefill,
   speculative verify) on int8 tensor cores, ordered so that every token gets the same
   bits as the one-token step. `src/cuda/mod.rs` and `ffi.rs` load the driver and NVRTC.
8. **`src/hybrid.rs`**: a model split across devices: the first layers on the CPU, the
   rest and the head on the GPU, one hidden-state copy between them per token; for
   prompts, the CPU layers' weights can be streamed through the GPU instead.

//! KV cache storage: f16 by default (half the bytes decode attention streams
//! per token), f32 with AXON_KV=f32. Values are rounded to f16 once, when

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
#[repr(transparent)]

///
/// # Safety
/// Plain data: every bit pattern (in particular all zeros) is a valid value,
/// alignment <= 64.
pub unsafe trait KvElem: Copy + Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn to_f32(self) -> f32;
    fn from_f32(x: f32) -> Self;

    /// dst[i] = from_f32(src[i]).
    fn store(dst: &mut [Self], src: &[f32]) {
        assert_eq!(dst.len(), src.len(), "kv store: length");
        for (d, &s) in dst.iter_mut().zip(src) {
            *d = Self::from_f32(s);
        }
    }

    /// The 8 values at p, widened to f32 (exact).
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// p..p + 8 must be readable, and the CPU must have AVX2 and F16C (the
    /// callers are x86-64-v3 code).
    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
    unsafe fn load8(p: *const Self) -> __m256;
}

// SAFETY: f32 is plain data, align 4.
unsafe impl KvElem for f32 {
    #[inline(always)]
    fn to_f32(self) -> f32 {
        self
    }
    #[inline(always)]
    fn from_f32(x: f32) -> f32 {
        x
    }
    fn store(dst: &mut [f32], src: &[f32]) {
        dst.copy_from_slice(src);
    }
    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
    #[target_feature(enable = "avx2,f16c")]
    #[inline]
    unsafe fn load8(p: *const f32) -> __m256 {
        // SAFETY: caller guarantees 8 readable floats.
        unsafe { _mm256_loadu_ps(p) }
    }
}

/// Largest finite f16.
const HALF_MAX: f32 = 65504.0;

// SAFETY: Half is a u16, align 2.
unsafe impl KvElem for Half {
    #[inline(always)]
    fn to_f32(self) -> f32 {
        crate::quant::f16_to_f32(self.0)
    }
    /// Saturating: |x| beyond f16's largest finite value (65504, inf
    /// included) stores +-65504, since one inf key or value would turn that
    /// head's attention into NaN for every later token. NaN stays NaN.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn from_f32(x: f32) -> Half {
        // f32::clamp passes NaN through.
        Half(crate::quant::f32_to_f16(x.clamp(-HALF_MAX, HALF_MAX)))
    }
    fn store(dst: &mut [Half], src: &[f32]) {
        assert_eq!(dst.len(), src.len(), "kv store: length");
        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
        if is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2") && is_x86_feature_detected!("f16c") {
            // SAFETY: AVX2 + F16C detected. Same bits as the scalar loop.
            return unsafe { store_f16c(dst, src) };
        }
        for (d, &s) in dst.iter_mut().zip(src) {
            *d = Half::from_f32(s);
        }
    }
    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
    #[target_feature(enable = "avx2,f16c")]
    #[inline]
    unsafe fn load8(p: *const Half) -> __m256 {
        // SAFETY: caller guarantees 8 readable halves (16 bytes).
        unsafe { _mm256_cvtph_ps(_mm_loadu_si128(p.cast())) }
    }
}

/// `Half::store` with F16C: the same bits as `from_f32` per element.
///
/// # Safety
/// The CPU must have AVX2 and F16C.
#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
#[target_feature(enable = "avx2,f16c")]
unsafe fn store_f16c(dst: &mut [Half], src: &[f32]) {
    let (sc, sr) = src.as_chunks::<8>();
    let (dc, dr) = dst.as_chunks_mut::<8>();
    for (d, s) in dc.iter_mut().zip(sc) {
        // SAFETY: 8 floats read, 8 halves (16 bytes) written, both whole
        // chunks. Saturate as `from_f32`: max/min return their second
        // operand when either is NaN, so x goes second and NaN passes through.
        unsafe {
            let x = _mm256_loadu_ps(s.as_ptr());
            let x = _mm256_max_ps(_mm256_set1_ps(-HALF_MAX), x);
            let x = _mm256_min_ps(_mm256_set1_ps(HALF_MAX), x);
            let h = _mm256_cvtps_ph::<_MM_FROUND_TO_NEAREST_INT>(x);
            _mm_storeu_si128(d.as_mut_ptr().cast(), h);
        }
    }
    for (d, &s) in dr.iter_mut().zip(sr) {
        *d = Half::from_f32(s);
    }
}

/// A zeroed buffer of `len` T in its own anonymous mapping: page-aligned
/// (so cache rows whose byte length is a multiple of 64 start on a cache
/// line), whole pages that no other allocation shares (a streamed prefill
/// page-locks each buffer on its own: `cuda::qwen2::stream`), and fresh
/// zero pages: untouched context costs no resident memory.
pub struct KvBuf<T: KvElem> {
    /// Owns the memory `ptr` points into (unmapped on drop).
    _map: memmap2::MmapMut,
    ptr: std::ptr::NonNull<T>,
    len: usize,
}

// SAFETY: KvBuf owns its mapping like a Vec<T>.
unsafe impl<T: KvElem> Send for KvBuf<T> {}
// SAFETY: as above; shared access is read-only.
unsafe impl<T: KvElem> Sync for KvBuf<T> {}

impl<T: KvElem> KvBuf<T> {
    pub fn zeroed(len: usize) -> KvBuf<T> {
        let bytes = len
            .checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<T>())
            .expect("kv cache size");
        let mut map =
            memmap2::MmapMut::map_anon(bytes.max(1)).expect("kv cache: anonymous mapping");
        // All zero bits are a valid T (KvElem); page alignment satisfies T's.
        let ptr = std::ptr::NonNull::new(map.as_mut_ptr().cast::<T>()).expect("mapping");
        KvBuf {
            _map: map,
            ptr,
            len,
        }
    }
}

impl<T: KvElem> std::ops::Deref for KvBuf<T> {
    type Target = [T];
    fn deref(&self) -> &[T] {
        // SAFETY: len initialized (zeroed) T at ptr, owned by self.
        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(self.ptr.as_ptr(), self.len) }
    }
}

impl<T: KvElem> std::ops::DerefMut for KvBuf<T> {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [T] {
        // SAFETY: as above, borrowed mutably.
        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(self.ptr.as_ptr(), self.len) }
    }
}

/// Per-layer K and V of one element type.
pub struct Layers<T: KvElem> {
    pub k: Vec<KvBuf<T>>,
    pub v: Vec<KvBuf<T>>,
}

impl<T: KvElem> Layers<T> {
    pub fn new(n_layers: usize, len: usize) -> Layers<T> {
        Layers {
            k: (0..n_layers).map(|_| KvBuf::zeroed(len)).collect(),
            v: (0..n_layers).map(|_| KvBuf::zeroed(len)).collect(),
        }
    }
}

/// The cache's storage, picked at `new_cache` time.
pub enum KvData {
    F16(Layers<Half>),
    F32(Layers<f32>),
}

/// A KV cache element type, as AXON_KV or `--kv` names it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum KvType {
    F16,
    F32,
    /// int8 with a scale per (position, kv head): the GPU only
    /// (cuda/decode.cu has the rule); the CPU has no q8 cache.
    Q8,
}

impl KvType {
    /// "f16", "f32" or "q8" ("" is the default, f16).
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<KvType, String> {
        match s {
            "" | "f16" => Ok(KvType::F16),
            "f32" => Ok(KvType::F32),
            "q8" => Ok(KvType::Q8),
            _ => Err(format!("unknown KV cache type '{s}' (f16, f32 or q8)")),
        }
    }
}

/// AXON_KV parsed (unset: f16), else a message for the user. `main` checks
/// it at startup.
pub fn kv_setting() -> Result<KvType, String> {
    match std::env::var("AXON_KV") {
        Ok(v) => KvType::parse(&v).map_err(|e| format!("AXON_KV: {e}")),
        Err(_) => Ok(KvType::F16),
    }
}

/// Whether AXON_KV asks for f32 (the CPU cache's choice; q8 is the GPU's,
/// and the CLI rejects it for the CPU).
pub fn kv_f32_setting() -> Result<bool, String> {
    kv_setting().map(|k| k == KvType::F32)
}

static USE_F32: std::sync::OnceLock<bool> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();

/// Whether new caches store f32 (AXON_KV=f32) rather than f16 (default,
/// or AXON_KV=f16), unless `set_f32` said first. Read once; the CLI has
/// already rejected bad values.
pub fn use_f32() -> bool {
    *USE_F32.get_or_init(|| kv_f32_setting().unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{e}")))
}

/// Fix `use_f32`'s answer (the CLI's --kv, which overrides AXON_KV), before
/// any cache is made; false if it was already decided.
pub fn set_f32(f32: bool) -> bool {
    USE_F32.set(f32).is_ok()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Buffers start on a cache line and read back zero.
    #[test]
    fn kvbuf_aligned_zeroed() {
        for len in [0, 1, 7, 1000, 1 << 20] {
            let mut b = KvBuf::<Half>::zeroed(len);
            assert_eq!(b.as_ptr() as usize % 4096, 0);
            assert!(b.iter().all(|h| h.0 == 0));
            if len > 0 {
                b[len - 1] = Half(1);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Saturating scalar rounding == the saturating F16C `vcvtps2ph` path
    /// (when the build has it) over a spread of every f32 class (stride
    /// sample of all 2^32 bit patterns, every half-way case near each f16
    /// exponent, values past +-65504, infinities, NaNs); widening is exact.
    #[test]
    #[allow(clippy::neg_cmp_op_on_partial_ord)] // up may be NaN past +inf: !(a < b) is intended
    fn half_store_matches_scalar() {
        let mut xs: Vec<f32> = (0..(1u64 << 32))
            .step_by(4099)
            .map(|b| f32::from_bits(b as u32))
            .collect();
        for e in 100u32..145 {
            for m in [
                0x1000u32, 0x1001, 0x0fff, 0x3000, 0x2000, 0x7f_f000, 0x7f_ffff, 1,
            ] {
                for s in [0, 1u32 << 31] {
                    xs.push(f32::from_bits(s | (e << 23) | m));
                }
            }
        }
        xs.extend([
            0.0,
            -0.0,
            f32::INFINITY,
            f32::NEG_INFINITY,
            65504.0,
            65520.0,
            65519.99,
        ]);
        // Beyond f16's range (saturate to +-65504) and NaNs of both signs,
        // quiet and signalling (stay NaN).
        for m in [65505.0f32, 65519.0, 65520.0, 65536.0, 1e5, 1e10, f32::MAX] {
            xs.extend([m, -m]);
        }
        xs.extend([
            f32::NAN,
            -f32::NAN,
            f32::from_bits(0x7f80_0001),
            f32::from_bits(0xffc1_2345),
        ]);
        xs.truncate(xs.len() / 8 * 8);
        let mut v = vec![Half(0); xs.len()];
        Half::store(&mut v, &xs);
        for (x, h) in xs.iter().zip(&v) {
            let s = Half::from_f32(*x);
            assert_eq!(h.0, s.0, "{x:e} ({:08x})", x.to_bits());
            let back = h.to_f32();
            if x.is_nan() {
                assert!(back.is_nan(), "{:08x} -> {:04x}", x.to_bits(), h.0);
            } else if x.abs() > HALF_MAX {
                assert_eq!(back, HALF_MAX.copysign(*x), "{x:e} not saturated");
            } else {
                assert_eq!(Half::from_f32(back).0, h.0, "{x:e}");
                // nearest: no other half is closer
                let up = Half(h.0.wrapping_add(1)).to_f32();
                assert!(!((up - x).abs() < (back - x).abs()), "{x:e}");
            }
        }
    }
}

//! `axon chat`: talk to an instruct model in the terminal.
//!
//! The whole conversation lives in one KV cache. A turn feeds only what is
//! new since the last one (the previous reply's end marker, then the user's
//! message), so a reply starts after a prefill of what was just typed, not of
//! the whole conversation. Qwen2's ChatML framing:
//!
//! ```text
//! <|im_start|>system\n{system}<|im_end|>\n
//! <|im_start|>user\n{message}<|im_end|>\n
//! <|im_start|>assistant\n{reply}<|im_end|>\n
//! ...
//! ```
//!
//! For text with no special-token strings in it, these are the tokens the
//! model's own chat template gives: the markers are special tokens and each
//! piece of text between two markers is encoded on its own, as a tokenizer
//! splitting the rendered template at special tokens does. Unlike rendering
//! then tokenizing, user text is never scanned for special tokens, so typing
//! `<|im_end|>` can't forge a turn. Replies stay in the history as the tokens
//! the model picked, not re-encoded from their text.
//!
//! Qwen3 (a vocabulary with `<think>`/`</think>`): no system block unless one
//! is given, and replies open with the model's reasoning, `<think>...</think>`.
//! `no_think` opens the reply with an empty `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n` instead
//! (the template's enable_thinking=false). As the template renders earlier
//! turns, a closed reply keeps only what follows its `</think>` (leading
//! newlines dropped); the next turn feeds it again from there.
//!
//! Llama 3 (a vocabulary with `<|start_header_id|>`): the official 3.1/3.2
//! template, without tools, its default date:
//!
//! ```text
//! <|begin_of_text|><|start_header_id|>system<|end_header_id|>\n\n
//! Cutting Knowledge Date: December 2023\nToday Date: 26 Jul 2024\n\n{system}<|eot_id|>
//! <|start_header_id|>user<|end_header_id|>\n\n{message}<|eot_id|>
//! <|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|>\n\n{reply}<|eot_id|>
//! ```
//!
//! (no newlines between the blocks; the system block is always there,
//! messages are trimmed as the template trims them).

use crate::lm::Lm;
use crate::sample::Sampler;
use crate::spec::PromptLookup;
use crate::tokenizer::Tokenizer;
use crate::{GenOpts, generate};
use std::io;
use std::time::Instant;

/// Qwen2.5's chat template uses this when the conversation has no system message.
pub const DEFAULT_SYSTEM: &str =
    "You are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are a helpful assistant.";

/// Llama 3's system block opens with these lines (the template's default
/// date, so a conversation's tokens don't depend on the day).
pub const LLAMA3_SYSTEM_HEAD: &str =
    "Cutting Knowledge Date: December 2023\nToday Date: 26 Jul 2024\n\n";

/// A chat format's marker tokens.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub enum Format {
    /// Qwen's ChatML.
    ChatMl,
    /// Llama 3's headers: `<|start_header_id|>`, `<|end_header_id|>` and
    /// the BOS token the conversation starts with (if the model adds one).
    Llama3 {
        start: u32,
        end: u32,
        bos: Option<u32>,
    },
}

/// How a vocabulary's conversations are framed: the format, its turn
/// opener and end-of-turn marker, and the tokens that end a reply. `axon
/// chat` and `axon serve` both frame through it, so they give the same tokens.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct Framing {
    pub format: Format,
    /// ChatML's `<|im_start|>` (Llama 3: its start header).
    pub im_start: u32,
    /// The end-of-turn marker: ChatML's `<|im_end|>`, Llama 3's `<|eot_id|>`.
    pub im_end: u32,
    /// Any of these ends a reply: `eos`, the end-of-turn marker, the
    /// tokenizer's end-of-generation set and `<|endoftext|>`.
    pub stop: Vec<u32>,
}

impl Framing {
    /// Llama 3 if the vocabulary has its header tokens, else ChatML; None
    /// if it has neither (not an instruct model).
    pub fn new(tok: &Tokenizer) -> Option<Framing> {
        let llama = (
            special(tok, "<|start_header_id|>"),
            special(tok, "<|end_header_id|>"),
            special(tok, "<|eot_id|>"),
        );
        let (format, im_start, im_end) = if let (Some(start), Some(end), Some(eot)) = llama {
            let bos = tok.bos();
            (Format::Llama3 { start, end, bos }, start, eot)
        } else if let (Some(im_start), Some(im_end)) =
            (special(tok, "<|im_start|>"), special(tok, "<|im_end|>"))
        {
            (Format::ChatMl, im_start, im_end)
        } else {
            return None;
        };
        let mut stop = vec![tok.eos(), im_end];
        stop.extend(tok.eog());
        stop.extend(special(tok, "<|endoftext|>"));
        stop.sort_unstable();
        stop.dedup();
        Some(Framing {
            format,
            im_start,
            im_end,
            stop,
        })
    }

    /// A message: `<|im_start|>{role}\n{text}<|im_end|>\n`, then the opening
    /// of `next` if given. Llama 3: `<|start_header_id|>{role}
    /// <|end_header_id|>\n\n{text}<|eot_id|>` (text trimmed), then the
    /// opening of `next`.
    pub fn frame(&self, tok: &Tokenizer, role: &str, text: &str, next: Option<&str>) -> Vec<u32> {
        let Format::Llama3 { start, end, .. } = self.format else {
            return frame(tok, self.im_start, self.im_end, role, text, next);
        };
        let mut t = vec![start];
        t.extend(tok.encode(role));
        t.push(end);
        t.extend(tok.encode(&format!("\n\n{}", text.trim())));
        t.push(self.im_end);
        if let Some(r) = next {
            t.extend(self.opening(tok, r));
        }
        t
    }

    /// The opening of a `role` message (the reply's, before the model's
    /// tokens): `<|im_start|>{role}\n`; Llama 3 `<|start_header_id|>{role}
    /// <|end_header_id|>\n\n`.
    pub fn opening(&self, tok: &Tokenizer, role: &str) -> Vec<u32> {
        let mut t = vec![self.im_start];
        match self.format {
            Format::ChatMl => t.extend(tok.encode(&format!("{role}\n"))),
            Format::Llama3 { end, .. } => {
                t.extend(tok.encode(role));
                t.push(end);
                t.extend(tok.encode("\n\n"));
            }
        }
        t
    }

    /// What a conversation starts with. ChatML: the system message framed,
    /// or nothing for None. Llama 3, always: BOS, then the system block
    /// with its date lines (the message trimmed, empty for None).
    pub fn system(&self, tok: &Tokenizer, system: Option<&str>) -> Vec<u32> {
        match self.format {
            Format::ChatMl => system.map_or(Vec::new(), |s| self.frame(tok, "system", s, None)),
            Format::Llama3 { start, end, bos } => {
                let mut t: Vec<u32> = bos.into_iter().collect();
                t.push(start);
                t.extend(tok.encode("system"));
                t.push(end);
                let text = system.unwrap_or("").trim();
                t.extend(tok.encode(&format!("\n\n{LLAMA3_SYSTEM_HEAD}{text}")));
                t.push(self.im_end);
                t
            }
        }
    }

    /// What closes a reply: the end marker, and a newline in ChatML.
    pub fn closing(&self, tok: &Tokenizer) -> Vec<u32> {
        let mut t = vec![self.im_end];
        if self.format == Format::ChatMl {
            t.extend(tok.encode("\n"));
        }
        t
    }
}

/// What one `Chat::reply` did.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Reply {
    /// The reply's tokens, a stop token excluded.
    pub ids: Vec<u32>,
    /// Tokens fed before the reply (new to the cache this turn), and the seconds that took.
    pub prompt_tokens: usize,
    pub prompt_secs: f64,
    /// Tokens picked (a final stop token included) and seconds spent picking them.
    pub decided: usize,
    pub decode_secs: f64,
    /// Draft tokens verified, and how many the model agreed with.
    pub drafted: usize,
    pub accepted: usize,
    /// Oldest exchanges forgotten to make room for this one.
    pub dropped: usize,
    /// The reply hit its token limit (`max_reply` or the context) before a stop token.
    pub cut: bool,
    /// `cancel` stopped it.
    pub interrupted: bool,
}

pub struct Chat<'a, M: Lm> {
    net: &'a M,
    tok: &'a Tokenizer,
    cache: M::Cache,
    ctx: usize,
    /// Every token of the conversation, in cache order: the system block,
    /// then one block per exchange (user message, reply, end marker).
    hist: Vec<u32>,
    /// hist[..fed] is in the cache; the rest still has to be fed.
    fed: usize,
    /// Length of the system block, hist[..sys].
    sys: usize,
    /// Where each exchange starts in hist.
    turns: Vec<usize>,
    lookup: PromptLookup,
    /// The format's markers; `fr.stop` ends a reply.
    fr: Framing,
    /// `</think>` and the empty reasoning block `no_think` opens a reply
    /// with, if the vocabulary has thinking tokens (Qwen3).
    think: Option<(u32, Vec<u32>)>,
    /// Open replies with an empty reasoning block (no thinking).
    pub no_think: bool,
    /// Most tokens per reply.
    pub max_reply: usize,
    /// Draft tokens per pass (`round_draft`ed for prompt lookup); 0 = off.
    pub max_draft: usize,
    /// Guesses from a draft model instead of prompt lookup (draft.rs). It
    /// follows the history by itself, edits included (`drop_oldest`, the
    /// reasoning cut): nothing here resets it.
    pub drafter: Option<Box<dyn crate::draft::Draft + 'a>>,
    /// How replies pick tokens (its RNG runs on across replies); None = greedy.
    pub sampler: Option<Sampler>,
}

/// `<|im_start|>{role}\n{text}<|im_end|>\n`, then `<|im_start|>{next}\n` if
/// given: the reply's opening (ChatML's `Framing::frame`).
pub fn frame(
    tok: &Tokenizer,
    im_start: u32,
    im_end: u32,
    role: &str,
    text: &str,
    next: Option<&str>,
) -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut t = vec![im_start];
    t.extend(tok.encode(&format!("{role}\n{text}")));
    t.push(im_end);
    t.extend(tok.encode("\n"));
    if let Some(r) = next {
        t.push(im_start);
        t.extend(tok.encode(&format!("{r}\n")));
    }
    t
}

/// The id of a special token, if the vocabulary has it as one.
pub fn special(tok: &Tokenizer, s: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    match tok.encode_special(s)[..] {
        [id] if tok.encode(s) != [id] => Some(id),
        _ => None,
    }
}

impl<'a, M: Lm> Chat<'a, M> {
    /// A conversation with `system` as the system message (None: no system
    /// block), in a cache of `ctx` positions. Err if the vocabulary has no
    /// ChatML markers. The net and tokenizer are borrowed: conversations can
    /// share them.
    pub fn new(
        net: &'a M,
        tok: &'a Tokenizer,
        system: Option<&str>,
        ctx: usize,
    ) -> Result<Chat<'a, M>, String> {
        let Some(fr) = Framing::new(tok) else {
            return Err(
                "the vocabulary has neither ChatML (<|im_start|>/<|im_end|>) nor Llama 3 \
                        (<|start_header_id|>/<|eot_id|>) chat tokens; chat needs an instruct model"
                    .into(),
            );
        };
        let think = match (special(tok, "<think>"), special(tok, "</think>")) {
            (Some(_), Some(end)) => Some((end, tok.encode_special("<think>\n\n</think>\n\n"))),
            _ => None,
        };
        let cache = net.new_cache(ctx);
        let mut c = Chat {
            net,
            tok,
            cache,
            ctx,
            hist: Vec::new(),
            fed: 0,
            sys: 0,
            turns: Vec::new(),
            lookup: PromptLookup::new(),
            fr,
            think,
            no_think: false,
            max_reply: usize::MAX,
            max_draft: 0,
            drafter: None,
            sampler: None,
        };
        c.set_system(system)?;
        Ok(c)
    }

    /// Positions in use, and the cache size.
    pub fn used(&self) -> (usize, usize) {
        (self.hist.len(), self.ctx)
    }

    /// A message, then the opening of `next` if given (`Framing::frame`).
    fn frame(&self, role: &str, text: &str, next: Option<&str>) -> Vec<u32> {
        self.fr.frame(self.tok, role, text, next)
    }

    /// What closes a reply (`Framing::closing`).
    fn closing(&self) -> Vec<u32> {
        self.fr.closing(self.tok)
    }

    /// Forget the exchanges, keep the system message (still cached).
    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
        self.hist.truncate(self.sys);
        self.fed = self.fed.min(self.sys);
        self.turns.clear();
        self.lookup = PromptLookup::new();
    }

    /// Whether the model has thinking tokens (`no_think` applies).
    pub fn thinks(&self) -> bool {
        self.think.is_some()
    }

    /// A new system message (None: none); forgets the exchanges. The cache
    /// keeps whatever prefix the old and new system blocks share.
    pub fn set_system(&mut self, system: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), String> {
        let sys = self.fr.system(self.tok, system);
        if sys.len() >= self.ctx {
            return Err(format!(
                "the system message is {} tokens, the context only {}",
                sys.len(),
                self.ctx
            ));
        }
        let same = sys
            .iter()
            .zip(&self.hist)
            .take_while(|(a, b)| a == b)
            .count();
        self.fed = self.fed.min(same);
        self.hist = sys;
        self.sys = self.hist.len();
        self.turns.clear();
        self.lookup = PromptLookup::new();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Forget the oldest exchange. Positions shift, so everything after the
    /// system block has to be fed again.
    fn drop_oldest(&mut self) {
        let end = self.turns.get(1).copied().unwrap_or(self.hist.len());
        let n = end - self.sys;
        self.hist.drain(self.sys..end);
        self.turns.remove(0);
        for t in &mut self.turns {
            *t -= n;
        }
        self.fed = self.fed.min(self.sys);
        self.lookup = PromptLookup::new();
    }

    /// Answer `msg`. Each reply token goes to `emit` as it is picked; an
    /// error from `emit` ends the turn and is returned (the exchange is then
    /// kept up to the tokens emitted). `cancel` is polled between prefill
    /// batches and before each token: true stops the turn, a stop before
    /// the reply's first token drops the message from the conversation
    /// (exchanges already forgotten to make room for it stay forgotten).
    pub fn reply(
        &mut self,
        msg: &str,
        cancel: &dyn Fn() -> bool,
        emit: &mut dyn FnMut(u32) -> io::Result<()>,
    ) -> io::Result<Reply> {
        let mut r = Reply::default();
        let mut user = self.frame("user", msg, Some("assistant"));
        // Where the reply (reasoning block included) starts, in `user` terms.
        let opened = user.len();
        if let Some((_, empty)) = self.think.as_ref().filter(|_| self.no_think) {
            user.extend_from_slice(empty);
        }
        // Closing a reply takes its end marker (and ChatML a newline).
        let close = self.closing().len();
        let fixed = self.sys + user.len() + close;
        if fixed + 1 > self.ctx {
            return Err(io::Error::other(format!(
                "the message is {} tokens; with the system message that leaves no room \
                 for a reply in a context of {} (--ctx)",
                user.len(),
                self.ctx
            )));
        }
        // Room for a full reply (up to a quarter of the context if replies
        // are unlimited), forgetting the oldest exchanges if need be.
        let want = self.max_reply.min(self.ctx / 4).max(1);
        while !self.turns.is_empty() && self.hist.len() + user.len() + close + want > self.ctx {
            self.drop_oldest();
            r.dropped += 1;
        }

        let start = self.hist.len();
        let turn_fed = self.fed;
        self.hist.extend_from_slice(&user);
        let n_gen = self.max_reply.min(self.ctx - self.hist.len() - close);

        // Feed what the cache doesn't have yet, in batches (cancellable
        // between them); the last batch with the last token, for its logits
        // (`Lm::prefill_logits`: on the GPU in the batched pass).
        let t0 = Instant::now();
        let pb = self.net.prefill_batch();
        let chunks: Vec<&[u32]> = self.hist[self.fed..].chunks(pb).collect();
        assert!(!chunks.is_empty(), "a turn adds tokens");
        let mut logits = Vec::new();
        for (i, batch) in chunks.iter().enumerate() {
            if cancel() {
                self.hist.truncate(start);
                r.interrupted = true;
                return Ok(r);
            }
            let pos = self.fed + i * pb;
            if i + 1 < chunks.len() {
                self.net.feed_batch(batch, pos, &mut self.cache);
            } else {
                logits = self.net.prefill_logits(batch, pos, &mut self.cache);
            }
        }
        self.fed = self.hist.len();
        r.prompt_tokens = self.hist.len() - turn_fed;
        r.prompt_secs = t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64();

        let Chat {
            net,
            cache,
            hist,
            lookup,
            fr,
            max_draft,
            drafter,
            sampler,
            ..
        } = self;
        let mut cancelled = false;
        let t1 = Instant::now();
        let res = generate(
            *net,
            cache,
            hist,
            logits,
            GenOpts {
                n_gen,
                stop: &fr.stop,
                max_draft: *max_draft,
                sample: sampler.as_mut(),
            },
            &mut |h, max| match drafter {
                Some(d) => d.draft(h, max),
                None => {
                    lookup.sync(h);
                    lookup.draft(max)
                }
            },
            &mut |id| {
                // Before the push: every token in r.ids went through the model.
                if cancel() {
                    cancelled = true;
                    return Err(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted.into());
                }
                r.ids.push(id);
                emit(id)
            },
        );
        r.decode_secs = t1.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
        let err = match res {
            Ok(st) => {
                r.decided = st.decided;
                r.drafted = st.drafted;
                r.accepted = st.accepted;
                r.cut = st.ids.len() == n_gen;
                None
            }
            Err(_) if cancelled => {
                r.interrupted = true;
                r.decided = r.ids.len();
                None
            }
            Err(e) => Some(e),
        };
        if r.interrupted && r.ids.is_empty() {
            // Nothing said yet: as if the message was never sent.
            self.hist.truncate(start);
            self.fed = start;
            self.lookup = PromptLookup::new();
            return Ok(r);
        }
        // Every reply token but the last went through the model (to pick the
        // next), the last too unless the reply was cut at its limit (no pass
        // goes past it) or `emit` failed on it. Close the exchange; the next
        // turn feeds the rest with its own prompt.
        let last_fed = err.is_none() && !r.cut;
        self.fed += r.ids.len().saturating_sub(usize::from(!last_fed));
        self.hist.extend_from_slice(&r.ids);
        if let Some((end, empty)) = &self.think {
            // The template renders an earlier reply as its text after the
            // last `</think>`, leading newlines dropped (or all of it if it
            // has none), without the empty block `no_think` opened it with.
            let at = start + opened;
            let ids = at + if self.no_think { empty.len() } else { 0 };
            let cut = match self.hist[ids..].iter().rposition(|t| t == end) {
                Some(p) => {
                    let mut keep = ids + p + 1;
                    while keep < self.hist.len()
                        && self
                            .tok
                            .decode_bytes(&self.hist[keep..keep + 1])
                            .iter()
                            .all(|&b| b == b'\n')
                    {
                        keep += 1;
                    }
                    keep
                }
                None => ids,
            };
            if cut > at {
                self.hist.drain(at..cut);
                self.fed = self.fed.min(at);
                self.lookup = PromptLookup::new();
            }
        }
        let closing = self.closing();
        self.hist.extend(closing);
        self.turns.push(start);
        match err {
            Some(e) => Err(e),
            None => Ok(r),
        }
    }
}

/// Ctrl-C while a reply is running stops the reply instead of the program.
#[cfg(unix)]
pub mod sigint {
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

    use std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize;

    static HIT: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
    /// The disposition `arm` replaced, for `disarm` to put back.
    static PREV: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(SIG_DFL);
    const SIGINT: i32 = 2;
    const SIG_DFL: usize = 0;
    const SIG_ERR: usize = usize::MAX;

    unsafe extern "C" {
        /// libc's `signal(2)`: BSD semantics on Linux (glibc) and macOS, so
        /// the handler stays installed and interrupted reads restart.
        fn signal(sig: i32, handler: usize) -> usize;
    }

    extern "C" fn on_sigint(_: i32) {
        // An atomic store is async-signal-safe.
        HIT.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    /// Catch Ctrl-C from now on; `hit` tells if it came.
    pub fn arm() {
        HIT.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
        // SAFETY: installs a handler that only does an atomic store.
        let prev = unsafe { signal(SIGINT, on_sigint as extern "C" fn(i32) as usize) };
        if prev != SIG_ERR {
            PREV.store(prev, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
    }

    /// Ctrl-C does what it did before `arm` again: quits, or nothing if it
    /// was ignored (nohup, a background job).
    pub fn disarm() {
        // SAFETY: puts back a disposition `signal` returned: SIG_DFL, SIG_IGN
        // or a handler that was installed.
        unsafe { signal(SIGINT, PREV.load(Ordering::Relaxed)) };
    }

    pub fn hit() -> bool {
        HIT.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }
}

#[cfg(not(unix))]
pub mod sigint {
    pub fn arm() {}
    pub fn disarm() {}
    pub fn hit() -> bool {
        false
    }
}

    /// Plain greedy from scratch over `ids`: what a reply after that history
    /// must be, by an independent path (fresh cache, one prefill, `forward`).
    fn fresh<M: crate::lm::Lm>(net: &M, ids: &[u32], n: usize, stop: &[u32]) -> Vec<u32> {
        let mut cache = net.new_cache(ids.len() + n + 1);
        let (&last, rest) = ids.split_last().unwrap();
        for (i, b) in rest.chunks(crate::PREFILL_BATCH).enumerate() {
            net.feed_batch(b, i * crate::PREFILL_BATCH, &mut cache);
        }
        let mut logits = net.forward(last, rest.len(), &mut cache);
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        while out.len() < n {
            let t = argmax(&logits);
            if stop.contains(&t) {
                break;
            }
            out.push(t);
            if out.len() < n {
                logits = net.forward(t, ids.len() + out.len() - 1, &mut cache);
            }
        }
        out
    }

        let (mut ag, mut ac) = (Agree::default(), Agree::default());
        for (max_reply, k) in [(12, 7), (64, 0)] {
            let mut chat = Chat::new(&net, &tok, Some(DEFAULT_SYSTEM), 2048).unwrap();
            chat.max_reply = max_reply;
            chat.max_draft = round_draft(k);
            let mut accepted = 0;
            for msg in MSGS {
                accepted += chat
                    .reply(msg, &|| false, &mut |_| Ok(()))
                    .unwrap()
                    .accepted;
                let hist = chat.hist.clone();
                let (&last, rest) = hist.split_last().unwrap();
                // The chat's cache, fed up to the last token as its next
                // turn would (then it carries on from there: positions past
                // the history are overwritten by the next turn).
                if chat.fed < rest.len() {
                    net.feed_batch(&rest[chat.fed..], chat.fed, &mut chat.cache);
                }
                let mut fresh = net.new_cache(2048);
                let before = net.streamed_chunks();
                for (i, b) in rest.chunks(crate::PREFILL_BATCH).enumerate() {
                    net.feed_batch(b, i * crate::PREFILL_BATCH, &mut fresh);
                }
                assert!(net.streamed_chunks() > before, "the fresh prefill streamed");
                let (cache, pos) = (&mut chat.cache, rest.len());
                compare_from(&net, &mut fresh, &net, cache, last, pos, 32, &mut ag);
                chat.fed = hist.len();
                compare(&cpu, &rows, &hist, 32, &mut ac);
            }
            assert_eq!(accepted > 0, k > 0);
        }
        report("0.5B cpu rows vs cpu (chat histories)", &ac);
        report("0.5B streamed chat cache vs fresh streamed prefill", &ag);
        assert_graded(&ag, &ac);
    }

    /// A small context forgets the oldest exchanges and stays exact.
    #[test]
    fn full_context_drops_oldest() {
        let Some(m) = crate::testutil::model() else {
            return;
        };
        let tok = Tokenizer::from_gguf(&m);
        let net = Qwen2::new(&m);
        let mut chat = Chat::new(&net, &tok, Some("Be brief."), 160).unwrap();
        chat.max_reply = 24;
        let sys = chat.hist.clone();
        let mut dropped = 0;
        for msg in MSGS.iter().chain(&MSGS) {
            let r = chat.reply(msg, &|| false, &mut |_| Ok(())).unwrap();
            dropped += r.dropped;
            assert!(chat.hist.len() <= 160);
            assert_eq!(chat.hist[..sys.len()], sys[..]);
            let prompt = &chat.hist[..chat.hist.len() - r.ids.len() - 2];
            assert_eq!(r.ids, fresh(chat.net, prompt, 24, &chat.fr.stop), "{msg:?}");
        }
        assert!(dropped > 0);
        chat.reset();
        assert_eq!(chat.hist, sys);
        assert!(chat.turns.is_empty());
    }

    /// The reply to the last message, from scratch: see `fresh`.
    fn check_last(chat: &Chat<Qwen2>, r: &super::Reply, n: usize) {
        let prompt = &chat.hist[..chat.hist.len() - r.ids.len() - 2];
        assert_eq!(r.ids, fresh(chat.net, prompt, n, &chat.fr.stop));
    }

    #[test]
    fn cancel_and_message_too_long() {
        let Some(m) = crate::testutil::model() else {
            return;
        };
        let tok = Tokenizer::from_gguf(&m);
        let net = Qwen2::new(&m);
        let mut chat = Chat::new(&net, &tok, Some(DEFAULT_SYSTEM), 64).unwrap();
        chat.max_reply = 8;
        let before = chat.hist.clone();
        let polls = &std::cell::Cell::new(0);
        let after = |n: usize| {
            polls.set(0);
            move || {
                polls.set(polls.get() + 1);
                polls.get() > n
            }
        };
        // Cancelled during the prefill: the message is dropped.
        let r = chat.reply("hello", &after(0), &mut |_| Ok(())).unwrap();
        assert!(r.interrupted && r.ids.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(polls.get(), 1);
        assert_eq!((&chat.hist, chat.fed), (&before, 0));
        // After the prefill (one batch: one poll), before the first token:
        // dropped too, though the prompt is in the cache now.
        let r = chat.reply("hello", &after(1), &mut |_| Ok(())).unwrap();
        assert!(r.interrupted && r.ids.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(polls.get(), 2);
        assert_eq!((&chat.hist, chat.fed), (&before, before.len()));
        // Too long to answer in this context: refused, nothing changes.
        assert!(
            chat.reply(&"word ".repeat(100), &|| false, &mut |_| Ok(()))
                .is_err()
        );
        assert_eq!(chat.hist, before);
        // Cancelled after 3 tokens: they stay, closed, and the next turn is exact.
        let r = chat
            .reply("Count to ten.", &after(4), &mut |_| Ok(()))
            .unwrap();
        assert!(r.interrupted);
        assert_eq!(r.ids.len(), 3);
        let r = chat.reply("Again.", &|| false, &mut |_| Ok(())).unwrap();
        check_last(&chat, &r, 8);
    }

    /// `emit` failing (stdout closed) ends the turn with its error, keeping
    /// the tokens emitted; the failing one never went through the model.
    #[test]
    fn emit_error_keeps_the_exchange_exact() {
        let Some(m) = crate::testutil::model() else {
            return;
        };
        let tok = Tokenizer::from_gguf(&m);
        let net = Qwen2::new(&m);
        let mut chat = Chat::new(&net, &tok, Some(DEFAULT_SYSTEM), 512).unwrap();
        chat.max_reply = 8;
        let mut n = 0;
        let e = chat
            .reply("Count to ten.", &|| false, &mut |_| {
                n += 1;
                if n == 4 {
                    Err(std::io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe.into())
                } else {
                    Ok(())
                }
            })
            .err()
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(e.kind(), std::io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe);
        assert_eq!(chat.turns.len(), 1);
        let r = chat.reply("Again.", &|| false, &mut |_| Ok(())).unwrap();
        check_last(&chat, &r, 8);
    }

    /// A new system message keeps the cache for the prefix it shares with the
    /// old one, and the replies after it are exact.
    #[test]
    fn set_system_reuses_the_shared_prefix() {
        let Some(m) = crate::testutil::model() else {
            return;
        };
        let tok = Tokenizer::from_gguf(&m);
        let net = Qwen2::new(&m);
        let mut chat = Chat::new(&net, &tok, Some("You are a pirate."), 512).unwrap();
        chat.max_reply = 8;
        chat.reply("Hi!", &|| false, &mut |_| Ok(())).unwrap();
        let old = chat.hist.clone();
        chat.set_system(Some("You are a poet.")).unwrap();
        assert!(chat.turns.is_empty());
        let same = chat
            .hist
            .iter()
            .zip(&old)
            .take_while(|(a, b)| a == b)
            .count();
        assert!(same > 3 && same < chat.hist.len());
        assert_eq!(chat.fed, same);
        let r = chat.reply("Hi!", &|| false, &mut |_| Ok(())).unwrap();
        check_last(&chat, &r, 8);
        // The same system message again: all of it still cached.
        chat.set_system(Some("You are a poet.")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(chat.fed, chat.hist.len());
    }
